title: Lecture 3 — Instructor Tutorial
subject: Algorithm Analysis
description: 16 questions transcribed from the instructor’s Tutorial 3: Iterative and recursive analysis, recurrence relations, and merge sort. Source questions, choices, and answer-key selections are preserved.

questions.question: If an algorithm contains neither iteration (loops) nor recursion, what can be concluded about its running time T(n)?
options: It is dependent on the input size n.
It will always be a constant value regardless of input size.
It cannot be analyzed using asymptotic notation.
It will grow linearly with the input size.
questions.correctAnswer: It will always be a constant value regardless of input size.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: It will always be a constant value regardless of input size.

questions.question: When analyzing a nested loop where the inner loop's iterations depend on the outer loop's index (e.g., for j = 1 to i), which summation formula represents the total number of basic operations?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: ∑(i = 1 to n) ∑(j = 1 to i) 1 = n(n + 1)/2

questions.question: What is the time complexity T(n) for a nested loop where both the outer and inner loops run from 1 to n?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Θ(n²)

questions.question: A recurrence relation is formally defined as:
options: A loop that calls itself until a stopping condition is met.
An equation or inequality describes a function in terms of its value on smaller inputs.
The process of converting a recursive algorithm into an iterative form.
A method used only to measure space complexity in fixed memory.
questions.correctAnswer: An equation or inequality describes a function in terms of its value on smaller inputs.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: An equation or inequality describes a function in terms of its value on smaller inputs.

questions.question: Match the following recurrence relation to its correct tight bound: T(n) = T(n/2) + c
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: Θ(log n)

questions.question: In the recurrence T(n) = c + T(n − 1), what does the 'c' represent?
options: The number of recursive calls made.
The time cost of non-recursive basic operations within the function.
The total depth of the recursion tree.
questions.correctAnswer: The time cost of non-recursive basic operations within the function.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: The time cost of non-recursive basic operations within the function.

questions.question: Which method of solving recurrences involves guessing the form of the solution and then proving it using mathematical induction?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects D: Substitution method.

questions.question: In a recursion tree for the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + cn, what does each node in the tree represent?
options: The cost of non-recursive work at that level of recursion.
The total space complexity of the algorithm.
questions.correctAnswer: The cost of non-recursive work at that level of recursion.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: The cost of non-recursive work at that level of recursion.

questions.question: For the recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + cn, what is the total height h of the recursion tree?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: h = log₂ n

questions.question: How many leaves are present in the recursion tree for T(n) = 2T(n/2) + cn once the input size reaches 1?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: n leaves.

questions.question: Merge Sort is categorized as which type of sorting algorithm based on its space requirements?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: Not In-Place Sort.

questions.question: What is the correct recurrence relation for the Merge Sort algorithm?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + O(n)

questions.question: During the space complexity analysis of Merge Sort, why is the total space complexity considered O(n)?
options: Because it only uses constant space for indices.
It combines the space for local variables O(1), the recursion stack O(log₂ n), and storing array halves O(n).
Because it sorts the array in-place without extra memory.
Because the recursion depth is n.
questions.correctAnswer: It combines the space for local variables O(1), the recursion stack O(log₂ n), and storing array halves O(n).
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: It combines the space for local variables O(1), the recursion stack O(log₂ n), and storing array halves O(n).

questions.question: What is the tight asymptotic bound for the time complexity of Merge Sort?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: Θ(n log₂ n)

questions.question: Which of the following describes an "Internal Sort"?
options: The amount of extra space required is constant.
Data is stored on a slower, external device.
All data to be sorted is stored in the computer's main memory.
The algorithm divides the input into halves recursively.
questions.correctAnswer: All data to be sorted is stored in the computer's main memory.
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects C: All data to be sorted is stored in the computer's main memory.

questions.question: When using the Back-substitution (Iteration) method to solve T(n) = c + T(n − 1), what is the generalized pattern after k steps?
questions.explanation: The tutorial answer key selects B: T(n) = kc + T(n − k)
